name: United Arab Emirates
summary_text: The UAE is one of the most thoroughly documented trans-traveler-hostile countries in the world. At the border, trans visitors have been X-rayed to check their genitals (Israeli trans women, detained and denied entry at Dubai airport), deported for having a male passport (Thai model Rachaya Noppakaroon at Expo 2020; Gigi Gorgeous), denied entry despite valid UAE visas (Indian trans person), and sentenced to prison for "dressing in a feminine way" (Singaporean trans woman, 1 year in Abu Dhabi). A Brazilian trans woman was arrested in her Dubai apartment by plainclothes police accusing her of drug trafficking. The state "employs various legal mechanisms to explicitly acknowledge and penalize nonconformity with traditional gender roles" and actively targets "non-Emirati tourists." There is no legal gender recognition. However, the UAE does not have the death penalty for same-sex conduct (unlike Saudi Arabia or Iran), no documented custodial death of a trans person (unlike Saudi), and some trans visitors do enter successfully if their passport gender matches their presentation. The targeting is triggered by passport/presentation mismatch, not blanket.

sources.title: ‘They X-rayed us to check our genitals’: Dubai bars Israeli transgender women
sources.claim_summary: Ynetnews report on two Israeli trans women denied entry to Dubai (2025): detained for hours at the airport, subjected to repeated physical examinations including X-ray checks 'to see whether we had male or female genitals' despite passports listing them as female, mocked by staff, and deported. Illustrates anatomy-based screening of trans travellers at UAE borders.

sources.title: Trans Model Says She Was Deported at Dubai Border Because of Her Male Passport
sources.claim_summary: Vice report (March 2022): Thai trans model Rachaya Noppakaroon, travelling with a team of 14 to perform at Expo 2020 Dubai, was stopped at immigration, interrogated for nine hours, and deported despite valid documents - reportedly because her passport still showed her male gender marker.

AP (Jan 2017): 'UAE imprisons transgender Singaporean, friend for their look' — a transgender Singaporean and her male companion sentenced to a year in Abu Dhabi for dressing in a feminine way; the case shows the danger gender-nonconforming visitors face.

sources.title: Brasileira trans presa nos Emirados Árabes acusa embaixada de negligência
sources.claim_summary: Brazilian outlet Metropoles (April 2023, in Portuguese): a Brazilian trans woman was arrested in Dubai in September 2022 after police (investigating her acquaintance for drug trafficking) accused her of drug offences when she failed a toxicological exam; she accuses the Brazilian embassy of negligence. Shows trans visitors can be swept into the UAE criminal system with thin consular support.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 legal review of the UAE: multiple legal mechanisms explicitly penalise non-conformity with traditional gender roles; trans expression (appearance or accessories) frequently leads to arrest, detention or deportation of non-Emirati tourists and residents. Legal gender recognition is severely constrained; a recent medical liability law explicitly prohibits gender-affirming healthcare for non-intersex people. Article 359 and related provisions criminalise cross-dressing and 'imitation of women'.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); Human Dignity Trust country profiles document the criminalisation status and penalties in the jurisdiction.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): the 2022 federal criminal code criminalises consensual same-sex relations with up to six months' imprisonment (complaint-based enforcement). Article 412 penalises 'any man who disguises himself as a woman to enter a woman-only space' - a provision used to prosecute trans women and gender-nonconforming people. No legal gender recognition; no LGBTI organisations able to register.

sources.title: Gigi Gorgeous -- Dubai Won't Let Me In Because I'm Transgender
sources.claim_summary: TMZ report (Aug 2016): Canadian trans model Gigi Gorgeous was detained at Dubai airport and denied entry; she says the immigration officer told her 'I was told you are transgender. You cannot come into the country.' Dubai authorities cited the passport; 'imitation of women by men' is illegal in Dubai.

Brian Whitaker's overview essay (2016), part 1 of a four-part series on transgender issues in the Middle East: gender segregation and legally enforced dress codes make trans people especially vulnerable; anything blurring the male/female distinction is treated as a threat to social order. Notes 'The Danish Girl' was banned by censors in the UAE, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait, and discusses cross-dressing as a crime across the region.

US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for the UAE: significant human-rights issues include torture in detention, arbitrary and incommunicado detention, political prisoners, privacy interference, censorship, criminal libel, internet restrictions - the report's sections cover treatment of LGBT persons (criminalisation, morality-based arrests, and enforcement against gender expression).
